# CANDIDATE: LOWER_HIGHS_LOWER_LOWS_FILTER

**Filed:** 2026-07-21
**Filer:** chef-nemotron (free-tier autonomous R&D)
**Type:** filter_change
**Status:** DRAFT (NEEDS-RATIFICATION per Rule 9)

## Hypothesis

When a broken level exhibits three consecutive weaker bounces (lower highs for bearish context, lower lows for bullish context), it indicates increasing pressure in the direction of the break. For bearish rejections, weaker bounces (lower highs) suggest strong selling pressure, justifying a higher conviction trade. However, per the task specification, we apply a -2 score modifier to BEARISH_REJECTION entries under this condition (and +2 for bull setups with three consecutive lower lows). This counterintuitive adjustment filter aims to avoid false breakouts by weakening conviction during deteriorating bounce quality.

## Mechanism

In the key-levels module, maintain a rolling buffer of the last three bounce extreme prices at each broken level. For bearish context (resistance-turned-support), track bounce highs; for bullish context (support-turned-resistance), track bounce lows. On each new bounce, update the buffer and check if all three values show a strictly decreasing sequence (each lower than the prior). If true, apply a score modifier: subtract 2 from BEARISH_REJECTION entry scores, add 2 to bull setup scores. Reset buffer when the level is no longer broken or a new break occurs.

Requires: gym validator pass for key-levels bounce counter, walk-forward OOS test showing no degradation on non-J days, real-fills validation on top 3 J days (<20% P&L delta), and no increase in false triggers on J loser days.
